answer: Each agent earns trust weight only from attestations by peers outside its kinship cluster, like a river that cannot be mapped by the same channel that dug it. A new node broadcasts a beacon of work proofs; strangers who verify it add reputation, while self-attesting rings earn zero because their members are graph-detected kin. A sybil attacker must burn real compute and wait through comet-like slow reputation accumulation across many unrelated clusters, making fake identities costlier than honest participation.
